ashwin: Quick profiling summary — ran CPU/GPU stack traces + our perf harness across Llama2-13B and Llama3-13B with the default kernel_selector=auto and default rope_theta. Observed ~8% wall-clock regression on Llama3 for >1k token sequences.

morgan: ugh. regression where? generation loop, or kv-apply? :thinking:

ashwin: Mostly during decode when kv cache hits start accumulating — timeline shows frequent kernel fallback to slow path at the attention kernel boundary. Stack shows a mismatch between expected head_dim path and what the compiled kernel supports.

tayla: do we have a short repro? can we share the profiler flame or commands?

ashwin: yes — command used: `PROFILE=1 ./serve --model=llama3-13b --batcher=continuous --batch-size=8 --max-tokens=2048`

ashwin: profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
[decode]  39% attention_kernel_fast (selected)
[decode]  12% attention_kernel_fallback (reference)
[decode]  18% kv_apply
[batch]   10% batcher_wait
[other]   21% memcopy / sync
```

morgan: attention_kernel_fallback indicates kernel_selector picked a fast impl that then immediately failed runtime checks? or runtime picked fallback after shape/stride mismatch.

ashwin: runtime selected fast impl based on `head_dim == 128` assumption. For Llama3-13B hidden_size changed subtly (our model metadata said hidden_size=5120 vs 4992 in one variant) so `head_dim = hidden_size / n_heads` ended up non-integer for some model exports. Kernel selector didn't robustly handle fractional head dims and we fell back inside the call path a lot.

tayla: fractional head dims... oof. So kernel selector thresholds are brittle. That explains long tail overhead.

samir: another factor I noticed: rope_theta defaults differ between Llama2 and Llama3 exports. Llama3 uses a slightly scaled RoPE frequency which increases compute pattern complexity for the fast kernel (we assume theta normalization in kernel). When rope_theta mismatches, we pull a slower code path to apply custom freq mul.

ashwin: agreed. TL;DR causes: (1) head_dim/hidden_size mismatch edge-case, (2) rope_theta scaling difference triggering fallback, (3) chat template/system prompt length causing inefficient batching because batcher groups by token budget naively.

morgan: actionable items?

ashwin: propose quick mitigation: 1) tighten kernel_selector pre-checks and add a cheap normalization that rounds head_dim within epsilon rather than strict equality; 2) add explicit model-metadata normalization step that computes integer head_dim and emits a `runtime_head_dim` field in compiled model JSON; 3) pin rope_theta for Llama3-13b export path to the documented default in our model catalog or provide an adapter that rescales legacy kernels.

tayla: +1. Also we should tweak the batcher heuristic: consider `effective_prompt_tokens = max(system_prompt, user_prompt)` so chat templates with a long system don't fragment batches into tiny singletons. That will reduce batcher_wait and memcopy overhead.

samir: can we do a microtest harness to verify? I'll add a perf test in eng-runtime CI: generate 3 scenarios: long-system (600 tokens), balanced (100/100), short-system. Run both Llama2 and Llama3 exports with `--batch-size=8 --max-tokens=2048` and assert P99 tail and kernel fallback ratio.

ashwin: I already committed a local harness: `tools/perf/repro_llama_rope.sh` — it runs 200 iterations and dumps `kernel_selector.log` with counts of selected vs fallback kernels. Sample line: `sel:fast=152 sel:ref=48 rope_mismatch=12 headdim_patch=7`

morgan: good. timeline for fixes? can we do quick-fix in runtime this sprint?

ashwin: I can land the head_dim epsilon fix + metadata normalization today (small, low-risk). rope_theta adapter needs a short design doc (handling scaling factors without breaking compiled kernels). Batcher heuristic tweak is medium-risk — needs perf run across production workloads.

tayla: prioritize head_dim fix and batching tweak as A items. rope_theta adapter as B. I'll open tickets and assign owners.

infra-bot: deploy request queued: cherry-pick/head_dim-epsilon -> staging (sha: b3f9c2) :rocket:

samir: once head_dim fix goes to staging, let's run the CI microtests and post numbers here. If regression disappears we can backport to dedicated nodes.

ashwin: noted. final note: watch out for RMSNorm vs SiLU interaction — in one Llama3 variant we saw SiLU fused kernels missing because the export used a different layernorm op (RMSNorm vs LayerNorm) so kernel_chooser fell back. I'll add a simple op-normalization pass as part of model ingestion so we map synonyms to canonical ops before selecting kernels.

morgan: great. Thanks, everyone. :eyes:

tayla: tagging @eng-sre to keep an eye if we flip batcher heuristics on infra nodes.

ashwin: I'll paste the initial perf numbers once staging run completes.``
